subject: english-literature
title: Blank Verse and Prose
welcome_lead: Shakespeare modulates between verse and prose for register, status and emotion. Hear the switch.
meta_desc: Blank verse, prose and verse-prose alternation in Shakespeare at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You can now hear the metre shifts — verse marks elevation, prose marks comedy, madness or low status.

concepts.def: Unrhymed iambic pentameter — Shakespeare's default for elevated dialogue and noble characters.
Non-metrical speech — used for comedy, low-status characters, madness, letters and informal exchanges.
Two consecutive rhyming pentameter lines — often closes a scene or aphoristic moment.
Shifts between verse and prose signal changes in register, status or psychological state.
Verse projects formality, ceremony and high emotion — Macbeth's soliloquies, Hamlet's introspection.
Servants, fools and low-status characters often speak prose; nobles speak verse.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Blank verse — unrhymed iambic pentameter — is Shakespeare's workhorse for noble speech. The Ghost in Hamlet, Macbeth's interior monologues, Othello's measured periods.

Departures from regular pentameter (a shared line, a feminine ending) carry interpretive weight.

When Hamlet feigns madness he often switches to prose. When Lear truly breaks his royal speech fragments into prose then back to verse.

Prose marks displacement — from court to inn, from sanity to disorder.
A rhymed couplet often signals a scene's close or an aphoristic punchline. Iago's I am not what I am rests in a closing couplet pattern.
